geo.title: What to know
geo.body:
Problem stations.

Goal: I can choose congruence or similarity for a problem.

  • 8.1 I can solve proportions and use the means-extremes property.
  • 8.2 I can dilate a figure from a center with a scale factor.
  • 8.3 I can verify that a dilation maps a line not through the center to a parallel line, leaves a line through the center unchanged, and multiplies every segment length by k.
  • 8.4 I can decide if two figures are similar using a dilation and rigid motions, and explain why all circles are similar.
  • 8.5 I can find missing sides using corresponding ratios.
  • 8.6 I can prove a line parallel to one side divides the others proportionally, and its converse.
  • 8.7 I can find the point that divides a segment in a given ratio, on a line or coordinates. (Supporting lesson for G.TS.2 and G.GF.7.)
  • 8.9 I can prove AA similarity from dilations and use it.
  • 8.10 I can use SAS and SSS similarity criteria.
  • 8.11 I can prove and apply the Triangle Angle Bisector Theorem.
  • 8.12 I can explain why areas scale by k squared.
  • 8.13 I can use scale factors to analyze a fractal.
  • 8.14 I can use congruent and similar triangles to solve real problems.

slides.title: Practice: 8.4
slides.html: Circle A has radius 3 and circle B radius 7.5. Describe a similarity that maps A onto B.
slides.reveal: Translate A's center to B's center, then dilate about it by 7.5/3 = 2.5.

slides.title: Common traps
slides.html:
Watch out for these common mistakes:

  • similar figures have equal sides
  • scale factor applies to area too
  • a dilation always enlarges
  • AAA proves congruence
